$Comment: The Yeti Cave, Christmas's repeatable fight: the den of the Yeti who scared off one of Santa's
reindeer. Bram the Shepherd opens it from his conversations while Christmas runs
(DialogueExtensions/SeasonsOfOrbis/Christmas_Yeti_Cave_Line.json). Every area of a copy pastes
Christmas/Christmas_Yeti_Cave.prefab.json, the game's own Yeti camp as the den with a snowy hall dug
out south of it, the Yeti's fight's entity, his spawn marker, the points his health packs drop on and
a way-out pad at the end of the entrance passage (tools/arena_markers.py writes it), so every fresh
paste stages a fresh fight. EntryOffset lands an arriving party on the passage's floor, 55 blocks
south of the prefab's anchor and 3 below it, and EntryYaw 0 turns them to face north, up the passage
toward the hall, with the Leave_Instance pad behind them. No intro camera plays.
Season keeps it closed outside Christmas. Share: one party to an area, up to five players, and four
areas to a copy. Complete names the Yeti's fight, so the run clears when he falls, and Rewards rolls
Christmas_Yeti_Cave_Clear for each member present as a Claim: full the first clear each day, half on
later ones. InChest puts that Claim in the chest the Yeti leaves where he fell, beside his own two,
so no results screen opens: each member sees a banner naming the clear with ChestKey's line under it.
A player who falls keeps everything they carry and wakes in this cave, beside their party. Text names
it in the reader's language (christmas.yeti.lang), and its GoalKey is the line each player reads as
they arrive: what to do there.
EntryCost is the price of going in: one Yeti Bait (Bram sells it at his stall once his reindeer have
their carrots), taken from whoever opens an area for their party; partymates who follow into that
fight walk in free. Confirm is left out, so it is on: before anything is spent, the player opening
the area sees CommonLib's confirm screen with the cave's name and description, the bait, how many
they hold and how many it takes, and a button whose words are ConfirmKey's; it spends the bait and
sends the party in, and closing the screen spends nothing. With none, the button is off and the
HintKey line says where Yeti Bait comes from. Change Count to change the price, and Bram's way-in
label, which names it, with it.
